claim: A model-constrained deterministic actor–critic method can learn a linear impedance-control gain that converges at steady state to the algebraic-Riccati optimal gain, while impedance indices can be selected using a stability map and transferred from virtual-force training to physical interaction tasks.
claim_locator: theory: steady learned gain and algebraic-Riccati solution
simulation: model-based versus neural actor–critic learning time
epistemic_status: Mixed theoretical and author-reported empirical evidence.
problem_and_setting: Accuracy-versus-flexibility impedance control under unknown interaction, evaluated in simulation and on a UR5 with ROS, a force sensor, and a 0.05 s control period.
method_or_mechanism: A linear or linearized discrete model augments robot state with force; a quadratic value function penalizes state, force, and control through impedance indices Qd and Qf. A model-constrained deterministic actor–critic learns a linear feedback gain. A Qd/Qf stability map bounds permissible external stiffness. Training uses a virtual constant force before selecting and transferring an impedance index to real tasks.
content_summary: The authors prove steady-state equivalence between the learned gain and an algebraic-Riccati optimal gain. Simulation reports about 100 s learning for model-based actor–critic versus about 1500 s for neural actor–critic. Hardware evaluation uses at most 10 episodes of 10 s. In wrist HRI, Qd=0.01 and Qf=1 is unstable during palm contact; retraining with Qd=0.1 stabilizes interaction but slows response. In grinding, Qf=0 yields about 40 N and surface damage, Qf=0.5 yields vibration and uneven texture, and Qf=0.2 yields near-constant force and a uniform surface. Applicability is primarily linear or linearized systems.
synthesis_role: Direct evidence for model-based impedance learning with analytically linked optimality and task-specific impedance-index tuning; a bounded linear-system baseline rather than evidence of deployment-safe exploration or broad transfer.
development_link: Supports embedding a dynamics model and stability-informed impedance-index selection while exposing unmet needs in nonlinear guarantees, environment identification, safe deployment exploration, and transfer.

evidence.finding: The steady learned linear gain is proven equivalent to the algebraic-Riccati optimal gain under stated linear-model assumptions.
Model-based actor–critic learns in approximately 100 s versus approximately 1500 s for neural actor–critic.
Qd=0.01,Qf=1 cannot maintain stable palm contact; after retraining with Qd=0.1, contact is stable but response is slower.
Qf=0 produces about 40 N and surface damage, Qf=0.5 produces vibration and uneven texture, and Qf=0.2 produces near-constant force and uniform surface.

boundary_conditions: Optimality proof concerns a linear gain for linear or linearized discrete dynamics.
Stability map relates selected Qd/Qf to permissible external stiffness.
Learning occurs under virtual constant force before transfer, not through safe deployment exploration.
Hardware evidence covers two UR5 tasks with at most ten 10-s episodes.
assumptions: Interaction dynamics are adequately linear or locally linearized.
Quadratic penalties and Qd/Qf encode the desired tradeoff.
Virtual-force training transfers to the task.
External stiffness stays within the stability-map region.

reported: Palm contact at Qd=0.01,Qf=1 is unstable.
Increasing Qd stabilizes contact but slows response.
Qf=0 grinding causes about 40 N and damage.
Qf=0.5 causes vibration and uneven texture.
Method is limited to linear or linearized systems.
inferred: No safe real-deployment exploration is established.
No external-stiffness identification guarantee is shown.
Collision/injury outcomes and nonlinear guarantees are absent.
Two tasks do not establish broad transfer.

verification_status: Controller-verified identity and content hash; findings limited to supplied full text.
